questions.q: What has to be configured before any change set can move between two orgs?
options: A Deployment Connection, with the target org allowing inbound changes and the source accepting outbound changes
Both orgs must be on the same Salesforce release
A Full Copy sandbox must exist between them
Nothing — change sets work between any two orgs automatically
questions.explain: Orgs must explicitly authorize each other on the Deployment Connections page before any change set can be uploaded or deployed between them.

questions.q: What does a brand-new Outbound Change Set contain immediately after creation?
options: All metadata in the org automatically
Just a Name and Description — no components yet
A pre-selected list of the most recently modified fields
A full copy of production data
questions.explain: Creating a change set only asks for a Name and Description; components are added as a separate step afterward.

questions.q: Why is clicking View/Add Dependencies important when adding components to a change set?
options: It automatically writes Apex test classes
It renames the change set to match Salesforce naming conventions
It catches related components a deployment would otherwise fail without, like a missing field or record type
It deletes unused components from the org
questions.explain: Dependencies are components the ones you added rely on — skipping this step is a common cause of failed deployments when a required piece wasn't included.

questions.q: What does the 'Run specified tests' option do when deploying a change set?
options: Runs every test in the org, including managed package tests
Runs no tests at all, regardless of environment
Automatically generates new test classes for any included Apex
Runs only the test classes you explicitly name, which must meet a 75% code coverage requirement for the included Apex
questions.explain: Run Specified Tests limits execution to named test classes, but Salesforce still requires at least 75% code coverage on the deployed Apex.

questions.q: What's the relationship between an Outbound Change Set and an Inbound Change Set?
options: They are two separate change sets that must each be built independently
An Inbound Change Set is a Salesforce-generated backup of an Outbound Change Set
The same change set is called Outbound in the source org and Inbound once it reaches the target org
Inbound Change Sets are only used for Full sandboxes, Outbound only for Developer sandboxes
questions.explain: It's one package viewed from two sides of the connection — outbound where it was built, inbound where it's received and deployed.
